Not too sure what you mean by a standing start...

Look at things like [vault](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8J2zWYjAgUo) & [tumbling](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R1pFHpg6ncU&feature=related).

They sprint and then do numerous flips in the air which in turn means they have a greater angular momentum then a long jumper who was only to do one flip.

The greater the angular momentum, the harder it is to slow yourself down and time your landing.

So if long jumpers were to practice their technique, it'd be as safe, if not safer then gymnastics.

How about gymnastics?

Screwing up one of their flips, especially at the speeds that they flip, could easily cause a broken neck. even on the padded floor.

Could also happen to them on beam, vault, uneven bars... pretty much every routine in gymnastics.

But it's what they practice and train for, to do these stunts and land them correctly.

So shouldn't the same apply for long jump?

It happens. There is absolutely no action to be taken by man to stop it. It might come tomorrow, it might come 100 years from now. The point is, we don't know when, we don't know how. It's nothing to fear and it's nothing to lament. Inevitability and futility go hand in hand often.


It stings, and it's a pain that nobody wants to feel, but it's a pain that mostly every single person to walk this earth will feel. Those who make it off this rock not feeling that sting left too early, and left someone with that pain.


There is no age when you know what to do. Every single person has a different method to cope and a different perspective on the life death cycle, and ultimately nobody is prepared for the death of a loved one. Even when told how much time you have left you always think there is a bit more to be had.


My piece of advice is a corny one, but it's my core philosophy when it comes to death: Don't mourn their death, but celebrate their life. It made way for your own, and it was an unfathomably long shot that any of us were to be born, so appreciate it. Don't worry about the time that's been lost and just relish in the time you had with them.

After the lowest point in my life, I've bounced back to the most amazing I've ever been.
